# What this year actually cost us

The launch is not what I'll remember. March is.

We spent eleven weeks rebuilding the ingest pipeline after Priya proved the retry path had been dropping roughly 0.3% of events since late 2023. Two migrations failed. The third held. Nobody asked for that work and it never showed up on a roadmap slide, which is exactly why it's the thing I'd point to first.

The numbers, since people ask: p99 write latency went from 890ms to 210ms. On-call pages fell from about 40 a week in January to 9 in November. We shipped the billing rewrite three weeks late and the audit log four months late, and only one of those hurt.

What we got wrong: the design system. Six months of effort, and half of frontend still hand-rolls components, because we never wrote the migration codemod we promised in the kickoff doc. That's on me. It's the first thing on the Q1 list.

Also worth saying plainly — we lost three people, two to other teams and one out of the company. Hiring backfilled two. The gap showed up as slower reviews rather than missed dates, and I don't think we talked about it enough.

Next year I want fewer things in flight. Six teams, four initiatives, and a real answer to who owns the platform layer. If you have opinions about that last one, my calendar is open and mostly empty on Thursdays.

Thanks for a hard, good year.

---
